headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell overlap: AutoGen can execute code and write files, while ms-swift also writes files and sends data to third-party model APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write working directories and uses stdin/stdout plus tool calls; ms-swift also reads/writes files and uses CLI/Python workflows. A shared workspace makes file-based instruction smuggling plausible, but no MCP or clipboard bridge is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same working directory or mounted volume
IF either agent treats file contents as trusted instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Disable automatic execution of instructions found in files
Add a human review step before copying outputs between agents
Prefix untrusted files with a quarantine label
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files and handle sensitive inputs: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and application data, while ms-swift handles hub_token/sdk-token plus datasets, checkpoints, and logs. If they share a workspace, either can expose the other's data through files or logs; no built-in isolation is documented for the pair.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same filesystem path
IF logs, checkpoints, or configuration files contain secrets or sensitive application data
mitigations: Store secrets outside shared workspaces
Rotate any exposed API keys or hub tokens
Restrict file permissions on logs and checkpoints
Separate datasets from agent scratch space
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted shell execution, subprocess spawning, and filesystem write access. AutoGen explicitly supports multiple instances with developer-defined shared state, while ms-swift does not state locking or isolation. Concurrent writes to the same directory can corrupt files or overwrite work, so the conflict is dangerous by default if co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or on the same mutable artifacts
IF no external lock or coordinator serializes writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Run only one writer at a time
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Snapshot the workspace before each run
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool-driven outputs, and ms-swift can consume CLI/Python workflows and model outputs. If ms-swift treats AutoGen output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream training, evaluation, or support actions; the pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly documented.
conditions: IF ms-swift consumes AutoGen-generated text or files as ground truth
IF no validation step checks citations, schema, or task success before reuse
mitigations: Require schema validation on exchanged outputs
Add a second-pass verifier before acting on AutoGen results
Limit AutoGen outputs to drafts only
Log and diff all handoffs between agents
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and application data, while ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files and can call third-party model APIs. If regulated or personal data is placed into ms-swift artifacts, retention and residency controls may diverge from AutoGen's application-data handling. The pair lacks documented compliance alignment, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in ms-swift logs, checkpoints, or datasets
IF the deployment requires a specific residency, retention, or deletion policy not enforced on both agents
mitigations: Classify data before loading it into either agent
Keep regulated data out of checkpoints and logs
Set explicit retention limits for artifacts
Review vendor/API data-processing terms
requires-engineering: align both agents to one compliance policy
